title: Integral torus fixed-point formula for coherent Euler characters
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], $H$ an affine $F$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme], and $T\subseteq H$ a closed split torus, meaning a subgroup scheme isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$. Put $X=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$, with addition given by multiplication of characters. Let $Z$ be an $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] smooth over $F$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and projective over $F$ [def-pc-morphism-conventions], with an algebraic $H$-action. Suppose its $T$-fixed subscheme is a finite disjoint union $P$ of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}F$ (the empty union is allowed); fixed means fixed after every $F$-algebra extension. Let $\mathcal E$ be an $H$-linearized vector bundle on $Z$, meaning a locally finite free $\mathcal O_Z$-module with an algebraic $H$-action on its total space, linear on fibres and covering the given action on $Z$. Then $H^i(Z,\mathcal E)$, computed on the Zariski site, is finite dimensional, vanishes for $i\gg0$, and carries a natural rational $H$-action: a coaction $V\to V\otimes_F F[H]$ satisfying counit and coassociativity. Its restriction to $T$, and every finite-dimensional rational $T$-module $V$, has a finite weight decomposition $V=\bigoplus_{\eta\in X}V_\eta$, where $v\in V_\eta$ means $v\mapsto v\otimes\eta$. Write $\operatorname{ch}_T(V)=\sum_\eta(\dim_F V_\eta)e^\eta$ in $R=\mathbf Z[X]$, with $e^\eta e^\xi=e^{\eta+\xi}$. At $p\in P$ let $\Omega_{p,j}\in X$ be the weights, counted with multiplicity, of the cotangent representation $(T_pZ)^*$, dual to the derivative of the geometric action. These weights are nonzero. In the localization $R_\Sigma$, where $\Sigma$ is generated by all $1-e^\eta$ for nonzero $\eta\in X$, one has
$$\sum_{i\ge0}(-1)^i\operatorname{ch}_T H^i(Z,\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\in P}\frac{\operatorname{ch}_T(\mathcal E|_p)}{\prod_j(1-e^{\Omega_{p,j}})}.$$
All coefficients here are integer dimensions. The assertion holds in every characteristic; no reduction of coefficients modulo $\operatorname{char}F$ is made.

proof.text: The structure map $q:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. Apply [lem-sfb-equivariant-coherent-proper-pushforward] to $G=H$, $q$, and $\mathcal E$. It gives finite-dimensional rational $H$-modules $H^i(Z,\mathcal E)$, zero for $i\gg0$, and their alternating class as $q_*[\mathcal E]$. Restriction to $T$ commutes with this operation by the same cited statement. Henceforth all Grothendieck groups carry only the restricted $T$-action.

proof.text:
By [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition], every finite-dimensional rational $T$-module $V$ is the finite direct sum $V= igoplus_\chi V_\chi$ of its weight spaces, indexed by group-scheme characters $\chi:T	o\mathbf G_m$, and $v\in V_\chi$ exactly when the coaction sends $v$ to $v\otimes\chi$. Characters of $\mathbf G_m^r$ are Laurent monomials: a group-like element $\sum a_
u z^
u$ in $F[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$ satisfies $\sum a_
u z^
u\otimes z^
u=\sum a_
u a_\mu z^
u\otimes z^\mu$ and counit $1$, forcing exactly one coefficient equal to $1$. Thus these simultaneous weights are precisely $X$. Equivariant maps preserve weights, so each exact sequence is exact on each weight space. Taking integer dimensions identifies $R(T)$ with $R=\mathbf Z[X]$; the inverse sends $e^\eta$ to the one-dimensional character module. Tensor products add weights, giving a ring identification. On the finite disjoint union $P$, a coherent $T$-module sheaf is a tuple of finite-dimensional rational $T$-modules, so $G_0^T(P)= igoplus_{p\in P}R$.

source.place: Theorem 22.50, p.480, general fixed-point input expanded by an agent using concentration and Koszul self-intersection; Example 22.36, pp.473--474 (integer formal characters).

proof.text: At $p\in P$, a tangent vector is an $F[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$-point reducing to $p$. It lies in $T_pP$ exactly when its extension to every algebra is fixed by every $t\in T$, which is exactly the assertion that this vector is in the invariant subspace $(T_pZ)^T$. Thus $(T_pZ)^T=T_pP=0$ since $P$ is a disjoint union of reduced points. By step 2 there is no zero tangent weight, and dualizing negates weights, so no cotangent weight $\Omega_{p,j}$ is zero. This uses the scheme-theoretic fixed functor, not fixed rational points alone.

source.place: Theorem 22.50, p.480, general fixed-point input expanded by an agent using concentration and Koszul self-intersection; Example 22.36, pp.473--474 (integer formal characters).

proof.text: Each inclusion $p:\operatorname{Spec}F\to Z$ is a section of the smooth structure morphism. By [lem-sfb-smooth-section-regular-immersion] it is a regular immersion near $p$. Remove the other finitely many closed points of $P$ when taking that neighbourhood. Thus $i:P\hookrightarrow Z$ is a regular closed immersion, with bounded local regular-sequence lengths since $P$ is finite. Its conormal fibre at $p$ is $\mathfrak m_p/\mathfrak m_p^2=(T_pZ)^*$, equivariantly, with the dual derivative action stipulated in the item. In a weight basis, wedges of subsets of the basis have weights equal to the sums of those weights. Consequently the $p$ component of $\lambda_{-1}(N^\vee)$ is $D_p=\prod_j(1-e^{\Omega_{p,j}})$, a unit in $R_\Sigma$ by step 3. The empty wedge gives $D_p=1$ in dimension zero.

source.place: Theorem 22.50, p.480, general fixed-point input expanded by an agent using concentration and Koszul self-intersection; Example 22.36, pp.473--474 (integer formal characters).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-torus-coherent-concentration], choose $\beta\in G_0^T(P)\otimes_RR_\Sigma$ with $i_*\beta=[\mathcal E]$. Apply the $R_\Sigma$-linear extension of $i^!$ from [lem-sfb-equivariant-regular-self-intersection]. The two identities in that statement give $\lambda_{-1}(N^\vee)\beta=[i^*\mathcal E]$. In the decomposition of step 2 and using the units of step 4, this is $D_p\beta_p=\operatorname{ch}_T(\mathcal E|_p)$ for each $p$, so $\beta_p=\operatorname{ch}_T(\mathcal E|_p)/D_p$. For $P=\varnothing$, concentration says that $[\mathcal E]=0$ in the localized group and the tuple is empty.

source.place: Theorem 22.50, p.480, general fixed-point input expanded by an agent using concentration and Koszul self-intersection; Example 22.36, pp.473--474 (integer formal characters).

proof.text: Apply the localized proper pushforward $q_*$ to $[\mathcal E]=i_*\beta$. By [lem-sfb-equivariant-coherent-proper-pushforward], $q_*i_*=(q\circ i)_*$. On each component $\operatorname{Spec}F$ the map $q\circ i$ is the identity, so this sends the tuple $(\beta_p)$ to $\sum_p\beta_p$. Step 1 and the character identification in step 2 identify the other side with $\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{ch}_T H^i(Z,\mathcal E)$. Substituting step 5 gives exactly the displayed formula. All groups and weight multiplicities used were integral, so this argument never reduces coefficients modulo the field characteristic.
